string.text: «100 SURVIVAL TIPS IN THE ZONE»
TIP №
Vodka is a cheap alternative to anti-radiation drugs and the most accessible way to reduce radiation levels in the body.
The properties of weapons, suits, or helmets can be improved by technicians in stalker camps.
The weight of your gear directly affects stamina consumption. Excessive weight limits mobility, and total overload will prevent movement entirely.
You can use filters in the PDA to hide or display different types of map markers. Filter controls are located between the map image and the active task line.
Some suits come with integrated helmets. Wearing other helmets with such suits is impossible.
You can safely wait out an emission in a sturdy building or underground. When an emission approaches, the location of the nearest shelter will be displayed on your PDA.
Flatness is a weapon parameter affecting the bullet's flight trajectory, while Handling determines how quickly the sights return to their original position after a shot.
To stop bleeding, use a bandage, an army medkit, or «Barvinok» drug. Unchecked bleeding causes significant damage and can lead to death.

The effects of medicine are not instantaneous, and some drugs have a very long duration. Note that the effect of the most recently taken drug overwrites similar effects from previously consumed substances.
Ask various stalkers about the current local situation, rumors, or stories—sometimes they can tell you something very useful.
To replenish your ammo supply, unload found weapons. To do this, right-click the weapon icon in your inventory and select the corresponding command.
To use an item quickly, drag it from your backpack to one of the four quick-access slots.
A detector is necessary for finding artefacts. More advanced models make the search easier and help detect rare and valuable specimens.
Some stalkers will refuse to speak with you until you holster your weapon.
Anomalies' boundaries can be identified by "probing" them with bolts. To prepare a bolt for throwing, press «$$ACTION_WPN_6$$».
Radiation is one of the most common dangers in the Zone. High exposure leads to rapid health deterioration and, without proper treatment, inevitable death.
Always check your food supplies before heading into the Zone; hunger or thirst can cripple your stamina at the worst possible moment.
There are drugs and food products that directly and positively influence your stamina and strength.
When heading out on a long expedition, double-check your essentials. Running out of medical supplies, food, water, or ammo will make your life significantly harder.
Running out of stamina can lead to a total loss of mobility at a critical moment, making you an easy target.
Visibility and noise levels can be monitored using the indicators in the upper-left corner of the screen.
Holding a detector in one hand does not prevent you from using a knife, pistol, or bolt in the other.
Certain medicines increase the body's resistance to environmental hazards and may be the only way to survive expeditions into deep anomalous zones.
A blood drop icon in the corner of the screen warns of bleeding. The color of the icon indicates its intensity.
A radiation symbol in the corner of the screen warns of dangerous exposure. The color indicates the intensity of the accumulated dose.
Relationships with those around you affect prices. Don't expect discounts if you have a bad reputation; conversely, good relations can grant access to unique goods.
A context menu is available for items in your backpack: hover over an item and press the right mouse button.
Most artefacts are radioactive. This effect can be compensated for by using other artefacts that absorb radiation.
The knife is ineffective against enemies with firearms. Its use is mainly utilitarian—designed for opening various supply crates.
A detector is the only reliable way to find artefacts in an anomalous zone.
Most artefacts are invisible to the naked eye until "highlighted" by a detector at a close enough range.
Night is the time of high mutant activity. Stalkers prefer to carry out their expeditions during daylight hours.
In case of heavy radiation exposure, use anti-rad drugs or see a medic. In emergencies, a medkit can slightly reduce the negative effects.
Guides can take you to remote locations quickly and safely, but their services are expensive.
Traders do not pay full price for items and will not buy gear that is in critical condition.
To repair gear, find a technician and click the repair button under the corresponding item in the upgrade window.
The AN-94 «Abakan» features a unique two-round burst mode. In this mode, both bullets hit practically the same point.
To detach attachments (scopes, silencers, grenade launchers), right-click the weapon in your backpack and select the corresponding command.
Double-barreled shotguns allow you to fire both shots almost simultaneously.
To move more quietly, use the walk key («$$ACTION_ACCEL$$») or crouch («$$ACTION_CROUCH$$»).
The shotgun is a close-quarters weapon. Its effectiveness drops to zero at medium and long ranges.
When choosing cover, consider the penetration power of bullets. Wooden fences and thin sheet metal won't protect you like a concrete slab or brick wall.
Do not underestimate pistols. They can be life-savers if your primary weapon jams or requires a long reload.
A direct hit to the head is fatal for most enemies not protected by heavy helmets.
Study mutant behavior. Knowing how a Snork or Bloodsucker attacks significantly increases your chances of survival.
The distance of a grenade throw can be adjusted by holding the aim button («$$ACTION_WPN_ZOOM$$»).
If you notice someone is about to throw a grenade at you, run for cover immediately. Shrapnel wounds are extremely dangerous.
By using a running jump, you can overcome significant obstacles and gaps.
Health and stamina indicators are located in the bottom-right corner of the screen.
Sniper rifles are ideal for eliminating targets at long distances but are extremely inconvenient in close combat.
Firing accuracy while moving is significantly lower than from a static position. For maximum accuracy, fire while crouching.
Worn weapons lose accuracy and begin to jam frequently, while a damaged suit provides less protection against bullets and anomalies.
The Zone is constantly changing. You might encounter mutants in an area you cleared just a few hours ago.
Anomalous fields may change their structure after an emission. Do not rely on old routes.
Artefacts can move slowly within anomalous zones. Be careful when chasing a "jumping" artefact—following it blindly makes it easy to fall into an anomaly.
«Hercules» drug temporarily increases your maximum carry weight, while psi-blockers protect your mind from psi-radiation.
You can find coordinates for stashes on some stalkers if they die.
Talk to stalkers in camps—you can learn about recent local events from their stories.
After each emission, there is a chance to find new artefacts in already explored anomalies.
Both primary weapon slots are equal. You can carry an assault rifle and a shotgun, or a sniper rifle and a machine gun simultaneously.
Specialized traders offer the best assortment in their field. Go to a medic for medicine, a trader for gear, and a bartender for supplies.
Medics in major camps often provide first aid for free or for a symbolic fee.
Personal boxes in camps are a reliable place to store loot. Stalkers generally do not steal from shared boxes at bases.
If you need to pass the time, use a sleeping spot in a camp.
Night Vision (NVG) is built into helmets, some suits, or scopes. Second and third-generation devices provide a much clearer image.
Listen carefully to your Geiger counter and anomaly detector—they will warn you of danger before you see it.
Always take a few spare magazines on a raid; there are never "too many" bullets in the Zone.
Don't forget to monitor the weather and environmental phenomena of the Zone, as well as the time of day—all of these can catch you off guard.
Study drug descriptions. For example, using a scientific medkit instead of a regular one can save your life from certain types of damage.
Flush enemies out of cover with grenades. But remember the shrapnel radius and try not to hit allies or neutrals.
You can drop almost any item without fear of cluttering the Zone; it will eventually disappear after some time.
Sometimes auto-saves occur upon taking or completing key mission stages; a notification will appear on the screen.
Upon returning from a raid, the first thing you should do is repair and restock. A second trip with a worn-out gun could be your last.
The game difficulty can be adjusted at any time through the settings menu.
Protection against anomalies can be increased in three ways: upgrading your suit, equipped artefacts, or taking specialized drugs.
Compare weapon stats before buying. A high rate of fire is good for close range, but accuracy and stopping power are more important at a distance.
Don't overestimate the explosive power of grenades; usually, one is barely enough to cause non-lethal shrapnel wounds to several opponents.
Artefacts aren't just for money; they are a way to acquire various anomalous improvements and characteristics.
Many objects are highly radioactive; do not approach them without anti-rad drugs.
Optical scopes with adjustable magnification allow for more effective fire at different ranges. Use the mouse wheel to zoom.
To switch firing modes, use the «$$ACTION_WPN_FIREMODE_NEXT$$» keys.
To crouch as low as possible, hold both the crouch and walk keys simultaneously.
Screenshots are saved in the game folder by pressing «$$ACTION_SCREENSHOT$$».
Use the lean keys to fire from around corners without exposing your entire body to bullets.
Don't be afraid to use binoculars—they are free and feature powerful, adjustable zoom.
At night, don't forget to use your headlamp or NVG if you have either available.
Try to stay neutral with all stalkers; you never know when a particular acquaintance might come in handy.
Anomalies outside of anomalous fields also change their location.
After an emission, there is a small chance you will find artefacts at the site of single anomalies.
The PDA displays not only the map but also message history—where you can re-read the details of an important dialogue.
To pull out your detector, press «$$ACTION_SHOW_DETECTOR$$». It will automatically be held in your left hand.
The pause menu allows you to think over your combat tactics without exiting the game.
A stalker or mutant caught in an anomaly has a small chance of generating an artefact.
Sprinting and frequent jumping lead to rapid exhaustion, but there are special jumping techniques that allow you to conserve stamina.
Learn to fire "from the hip" at medium ranges; with proper skill, this will make your shooting much more efficient.
Some weapons allow the installation of an under-barrel grenade launcher, which lets you send explosive gifts to unfriendly stalkers much further and more accurately.
There are various types of ammunition in the Zone; study each of them theoretically and empirically.
When an emission occurs, you have enough time to unhurriedly reach the nearest shelter.
Some anomalies and mutants emit dangerous auras that have a negative effect on you. Try to break distance from the source of such trouble as quickly as possible.
Most locations on the map must be discovered on your own. Roam as often as possible in search of something interesting.
Money and rating points are awarded for kills and artefact deliveries, unlocking access to more powerful gear.
In «Artefact Hunt» mode, the first team to deliver the required number of artefacts to their base wins.
In «Deathmatch» mode, it's every man for himself. Your goal is the maximum number of kills within the time limit.
Coordination is key in «Team Deathmatch». Loners quickly become targets for a well-organized group.
In «Capture the Artefact» mode, your task is to steal the artefact from the enemy base and bring it to yours.
If an ally carrying the artefact is killed, pick it up with the «Use» key to continue the mission.
An activated artefact creates a temporary anomaly that can block a narrow passage for the enemy.
A player carrying the artefact cannot sprint. Provide them with heavy cover.
The player with the artefact is visible on the mini-map to all participants of the battle.
Energy drinks in multiplayer allow you to pursue an enemy longer or escape from fire faster.
Smoke grenades are an ideal tool for covertly entering the enemy base.
In «Free for All» mode, ammo is infinite, but weapons still wear out and can jam.
The buy menu is divided into categories. The higher your rank, the more NATO and Eastern bloc weapons become available to you.
Use the quick-buy slots (floppy disk icons) to instantly purchase your favorite gear set at the start of the round.
Keys 2 and 3 allow you to quickly switch between your primary and secondary weapons.
Shooting limbs deals less damage. Always aim for the head or the heart area.
Be careful with artefact activation: the created anomaly kills everyone indiscriminately, including allies.
The «SEVA» suit provides excellent protection against player-made anomalies but is weak against bullets.
The AN-94 «Abakan» in multiplayer is a formidable weapon at medium ranges thanks to its two-round burst mode.
Weapon attachments are purchased separately in the equipment menu.
The mini-map displays the position of the artefact. The target's vertical position is indicated by an arrow next to the icon.
Quiet movement allows you to flank the enemy. Remember: sprinting can be heard from afar.
A shotgun in the hands of an enemy in a narrow corridor is almost guaranteed death. Keep your distance.
Material penetration in multiplayer is the same as in singleplayer. Hide behind concrete.
Pistols in multiplayer are often used as a "last chance" weapon when your primary magazine is empty.
A headshot from an SVD instantly takes out any player, except for Exoskeleton owners at full health.
Jumping and sprinting consume stamina. If it's at zero, you won't be able to quickly dodge a grenade.
A long grenade throw allows you to deliver a "gift" to the second floor of the enemy base.
If a grenade is at your feet, jump to the side. This can save you from lethal shrapnel damage.
Multiplayer maps are full of secret paths. Use parkour to take an unexpected position.
Health and armor are your main resources. Don't forget to buy medkits at the base.
Snipers on open maps are the main threat. Cross open areas only in zigzags or under smoke cover.
Shooting while jumping is absolutely inaccurate. Don't try to play the action hero.
Worn weapons can fail you at the most critical moment of a duel.
Artefact direction icons help you navigate multi-level maps.
Pick up the backpacks of the fallen—they might contain scarce grenades or an expensive rifle.
Protecting the artefact carrier is the #1 priority for the entire team.
When throwing a grenade, warn your allies to avoid a «Teamkill» penalty.
Use the voice command system (V, C) to quickly request support.
Voting to kick cheaters or change the map is initiated through the pause menu.
The score table (TAB) shows players' ping. High ping gives an advantage in sudden movements but hinders accurate shooting.
After death, you respawn after a few seconds. Use the time to plan your next purchase.
The buy menu is only available within your base zone.
Team chat allows for coordinating stealthy attacks.
Running with a heavy RP-74 machine gun exhausts the character in seconds.
Aiming mode reduces recoil and bullet spread.
An under-barrel grenade launcher is an excellent argument against a group of enemies at a capture point.
Different ammo types are effective in different situations. Hollow-point for "naked" enemies, armor-piercing for Exoskeletons.
Reload only in cover. The magazine change animation is your moment of maximum vulnerability.
Weapons dropped at the base can be picked up by allies who didn't have enough money for a purchase.
In the inventory, you can quickly transfer ammo to a teammate.
Use the 3-round burst on assault rifles for recoil control at long distances.
A low crouch allows you to hide behind low objects where a sniper doesn't expect to see you.
A headshot from a Desert Eagle pistol kills even through a good helmet.
Leaning allows you to fire while leaving only a small portion of your head exposed.
